That happens for two common reasons.

By default, React re-renders a child whenever its parent re-renders, no matter what props you pass. React only skips it if you wrap the child in `React.memo`.

Even with `React.memo`, the child still re-renders if any prop is a new function or object each render — like an inline arrow function or a `{}` literal — since those aren't the same reference twice, even though they look identical.

Fix: wrap the child in `React.memo`, and wrap any functions or objects you pass down in `useCallback` or `useMemo` so their references stay stable.
